summary: Research shows that speech and text elicit different content and that prompt detail can matter, but there is not yet strong controlled evidence that verbose spoken intent reliably improves software-agent outcomes over careful typed requests.

items.text: Speech vs Transcript in Automatic Summarization (ACL 2024) found modality-dependent differences in human summaries, with speech-based references more selective and factually consistent in the studied setting; this is adjacent evidence about capture modality, not a coding-agent trial.
A 2004 comparative study of spoken and written natural-language interaction reports systematic modality differences; its older dialogue/search setting limits transfer to modern LLM task intake.

A 2026 experience report on voice-based requirements elicitation with LLMs discusses practical opportunities and transcription risks; it is qualitative evidence rather than a controlled productivity study.
More than a Score (IJCNLP-AACL 2025) studies instruction quality in detail and supports treating specificity as multidimensional, while not testing voice input itself.
